diseases.name: Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot
diseases.description: A bacterial disease affecting peppers, causing small, water-soaked spots on leaves and fruits.
symptoms: Small, water-soaked spots on leaves and fruits.
Spots enlarge to dark brown lesions with yellow halos.
Severe infections cause leaves to drop, exposing fruits to sunscald.
prevention: Use disease-free seeds.
Practice crop rotation.
Avoid overhead watering to reduce leaf wetness.
remedies: Remove and destroy infected plants.
Apply copper-based bactericides as a preventive measure.
Avoid working in the garden when plants are wet to prevent spreading.

diseases.name: Potato___Early_blight
diseases.description: A fungal disease that causes dark spots on the leaves, often with concentric rings, leading to reduced yield.
symptoms: Brown circular spots with light-gray centers and reddish-brown margins on leaves.
Spots develop into large, tan, concentric circles resembling 'frog-eye' appearance.
As spots coalesce, large lesions form, often causing leaf drop and exposing fruits to sunscald.
prevention: Use certified, disease-free seed potatoes.
Practice crop rotation.
Avoid overhead watering and improve air circulation.
remedies: Remove affected leaves and dispose of them.
Apply fungicides such as chlorothalonil or copper-based products.
Maintain proper plant spacing for good airflow.

diseases.name: Potato___Late_blight
diseases.description: A devastating fungal disease that affects leaves, stems, and tubers, causing large, water-soaked lesions.
symptoms: Large, irregular water-soaked spots on leaves, often with a gray-white fungal growth on the underside.
Dark brown lesions on stems.
Tubers develop firm, brownish-purple decay under the skin.
prevention: Use resistant varieties when available.
Avoid overhead watering.
Remove volunteer potato plants and infected debris from the previous season.
remedies: Apply fungicides such as mancozeb or copper-based sprays.
Destroy infected plants to prevent spread.
Avoid handling plants when they are wet.

diseases.name: Tomato_Bacterial_spot
diseases.description: A bacterial disease causing small, dark spots on leaves, stems, and fruits.
symptoms: Small, dark water-soaked spots on leaves and stems.
Lesions with dark, scab-like appearance on fruits.
Yellow halos around spots, leading to defoliation in severe cases.
prevention: Use disease-free seeds and transplants.
Rotate crops to reduce bacterial buildup in the soil.
Avoid overhead irrigation.
remedies: Apply copper-based bactericides at the first sign of infection.
Remove and destroy infected plants.
Practice good garden hygiene by cleaning tools and equipment.

diseases.name: Tomato_Early_blight
diseases.description: A fungal disease that causes concentric rings on leaves and can lead to significant defoliation.
symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings on leaves, often resembling 'target spots'.
Yellowing of leaves around the spots.
Severe infection causes leaves to drop, exposing fruits to sunscald.
prevention: Use resistant tomato varieties.
Practice crop rotation.
Avoid overhead watering and ensure good air circulation.
remedies: Remove and destroy infected leaves.
Apply fungicides such as chlorothalonil or mancozeb.
Mulch around the base of plants to reduce soil splashing.

diseases.name: Tomato_Late_blight
diseases.description: A serious fungal disease affecting tomato plants, causing large, irregular spots on leaves, stems, and fruits.
symptoms: Large, irregular water-soaked lesions on leaves and stems.
Grayish-white fungal growth on the underside of infected leaves.
Fruits develop brownish-gray rot, often firm to the touch.
prevention: Use resistant tomato varieties when available.
Water plants at the base to keep foliage dry.
Practice crop rotation and remove volunteer plants.
remedies: Apply fungicides, especially in damp weather conditions.
Remove and destroy infected plants immediately.
Increase plant spacing to improve air circulation.

diseases.name: Tomato_Leaf_Mold
diseases.description: A fungal disease causing yellow spots on the upper side of leaves, with mold on the underside.
symptoms: Yellow spots on the upper side of leaves.
Grayish mold on the underside of infected leaves.
In severe cases, infected leaves may drop.
prevention: Use resistant varieties.
Water plants at the base rather than overhead.
Improve air circulation in the growing area.
remedies: Remove and destroy affected leaves.
Apply fungicides like copper-based sprays.
Avoid overcrowding plants to reduce humidity.

diseases.name: Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus
diseases.description: A viral disease transmitted by whiteflies, causing yellowing and curling of leaves.
symptoms: Yellowing and upward curling of leaves.
Reduced leaf size and stunted plant growth.
In severe cases, plants may not produce fruit.
prevention: Control whitefly population with insecticidal soap or neem oil.
Use row covers to protect plants from insect vectors.
Plant resistant tomato varieties if available.
remedies: Remove and destroy infected plants.
Regularly inspect plants for whiteflies and remove them.
Use reflective mulch to deter whiteflies.

diseases.name: Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus
diseases.description: A viral disease that causes mottling, yellowing, and curling of leaves, often spread by human activity.
symptoms: Mottled light and dark green patterns on leaves.
Yellowing and curling of leaves.
Plants may have stunted growth and reduced fruit production.
prevention: Use certified virus-free seeds.
Practice good sanitation by washing hands and tools before handling plants.
Avoid smoking near tomato plants, as the virus can spread from tobacco.
remedies: Remove infected plants and destroy them.
Avoid handling healthy plants after touching infected plants.
Control aphids and other insects that can spread the virus.

diseases.name: Tomato_healthy
diseases.description: Healthy tomato plants with no signs of disease.
